body.x: PCL Co., Ltd. (CEO So Yeon Kim) participated in the world’s largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition, CES 2024, held in Las Vegas, USA, from the 9th (Tuesday) to the 12th (Friday, local time).

PCL, which went public on the KOSDAQ in 2017, is a company developing in vitro diagnostic solutions. Through CEO So Yeon Kim’s nationally designated research laboratory project (supported by the Ministry of Science and Technology), the company has secured 3D immobilization technology for compounds and proteins. PCL presents new indicators for multiple immune diagnostics through the so-called ‘SG CapTM’ core technology.

In particular, PCL garnered attention by being the first in the world to launch a multi-immune diagnostic product for high-risk viruses. The company has also demonstrated advanced technological capabilities with the ‘HiSU’ system, a high-speed automated testing device, and an on-site diagnostic compact equipment named ‘PCLOKII.’

Furthermore, during the COVID-19 pandemic, PCL developed a self-diagnosis kit for diagnosing COVID-19 using saliva. The company achieved significant results by exporting these kits to 50 countries worldwide. Additionally, PCL has expanded its business into the AI-based medical electronics field, leading in the future of digital healthcare. The company has collaborated with Gangnam Severance Hospital and NHN Cloud to pioneer AI-based medical electronics, further broadening its business scope.

In addition, PCL has received recognition for its technological capabilities through various certifications and designations, including being designated as a Seoul-type specialized small and medium-sized enterprise, an innovative medical device company selected by the Ministry of Health and Welfare, a designated innovative prototype by the Public Procurement Service, and a family-friendly company certified for possessing national core technologies by the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy.

At CES 2024, PCL showcased its flagship product, the ‘Smart Healthcare Platform.’ This platform aims to go beyond traditional hospital settings by providing more accurate test results. The company anticipated that the Smart Healthcare Platform would lead medical diagnostic innovation by addressing issues arising from medical care delays during emergency conditions, such as cerebrovascular diseases.

Particularly, this platform boasts exceptional user-friendliness as a compact medical device usable at home. The product’s strengths include an AI-driven analysis process that enables early risk detection, timely diagnosis, and treatment.

body.cap: A glimpse of PCL’s disease diagnostic solution product line exhibited at the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, ‘CES 2024,’ held in Las Vegas on the 9th (local time) | Photo - AVING News

body.x: The collaboration with NHN Cloud and Gangnam Severance Hospital will aim to contribute to comprehensive data management and prevention of five major environmentally related diseases (Green Healthcare Cloud Platform). In addition, prediction and management services for chronic cardiovascular diseases can provide accurate risk assessments without the need for traditional testing systems, utilizing IVD devices and machine learning.

So Yeon Kim, the CEO of PCL, stated, “There is a growing demand worldwide for digital healthcare platforms that enable effective diagnosis and prediction of various diseases at home.” She further mentioned, “Our products will significantly impact countries where the universality of medical services is relatively low, as they offer more in-depth and advanced diagnostic solutions. Indeed, during this CES event, we received considerable interest from potential customers in regions such as Africa and Central Asia.”

CEO Kim said, “Although domestic laws currently restrict it, we anticipate that soon, there will be a time when diagnostic medical devices can be bought and sold like household appliances.” She added, “In line with this, we are investing our capabilities in developing more convenient and innovative products. It’s also gratifying to have the opportunity, here at CES, to meet with technology companies that can collaborate on product expansion and discuss future trends in the medical device market.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
